title: Peas on Earth
summary: A team web GIS project exploring food access and transit equity across Seattle.

notes.heading: The question
notes.text: How can a map help people understand food access in relation to Seattle's transit network?

notes.heading: The work
notes.text: I worked with a team on an interactive mapping app that brings civic data into one place. The project combines my interests in visualization, geography, and questions about the city I live in.

notes.heading: Take a look
notes.text: The published app lets you explore the map yourself. This was a team project, and the live site includes our shared work.

title: Campus Cop
summary: A campus safety reporting app built with a four-person team I led.

notes.heading: The question
notes.text: How could campus safety reporting be faster and clearer for students?

notes.heading: My part
notes.text: I led a four-person team as we built a web app focused on campus safety. It gave me experience connecting a user-facing problem with the decisions involved in building and shipping an app.

notes.heading: The build
notes.text: The project uses React and is deployed with Firebase. You can visit the live app to see the team's work.

title: Digital Age vs. Seattle's Homeless Elderly
summary: UX research into digital accessibility barriers for elderly, unhoused Seattle residents.

notes.heading: The question
notes.text: What happens when services move online, but the people who need them face barriers to digital access?

notes.heading: The work
notes.text: This project explored digital accessibility for elderly, unhoused residents in Seattle and what services could do differently. It brought a research perspective to how I think about designing useful tools.

notes.heading: Let's talk
notes.text: Contact me if you'd like to hear more about the research and the thinking behind this project.
